title: Chained withdrawals test (5+ sequential)
description: Test 5+ sequential withdrawals from same deposit. Likely impossible by design as child commitments use random circuit-generated secrets that clients never learn, preventing linkability.

comments.author: vitorpy
comments.text:
Child commitment limitation test implemented and passing (5 tests). Documents why chained withdrawals from child commitments are IMPOSSIBLE BY DESIGN:
- Withdrawal circuit generates NEW random nullifier/secret for child commitment
- Client never learns child secrets (cryptographically hidden)
- This is a PRIVACY FEATURE preventing linkability attacks
- Alternative workaround: multiple deposits from same user (already tested)
See: tests-package/withdrawals/child-commitment-limitation-test.test.js

title: State Integrity test: track commitment updates from withdrawals
description:
The State Integrity test's final withdrawal verification is limited because allDeposits array contains original commitments, but previous tests' withdrawals create NEW commitments (with remaining value) that replace old ones in the pool's state tree.

Current workaround: Using only fresh deposits from the current test for final withdrawal.

Solution needed: Either track commitment updates when withdrawals happen, or add helper function to rebuild merkle tree from pool state.

Location: tests-package/security/critical-security-tests.test.js line 432

comments.author: vitorpy
comments.text:
Solved with atomic test suite and root validation approach (commit 393a7fd).

The solution validates local merkle tree roots against on-chain state before building proofs, ensuring commitment tracking stays in sync with blockchain state. This eliminates the need for manual cross-test commitment accumulation.

New validateTreeRoots() helper in client/merkle.js queries pool state and validates roots, failing fast if divergence is detected. All atomic tests now use this pattern.
